A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Over-Tokenized Transformer research. All 20 pages of v1 and 22 pages of v2, including Appendices A-C, are readable and support comparison of text, equations, tables and figures.

before.justification: v1 reports original CFG experiments, OLMo2 and OLMoE training evaluations, and OE/OD ablations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds training/inference efficiency measurements and in-house model evaluations in Section 4.4 and Appendix B.5.

M1.justification: The hierarchical OE embeddings, hashing, slicing, MTP-DS integration and OD objectives remain unchanged, as do Algorithms 1 and 2. Equation (5) corrects an index to match the already-described procedure; it does not establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: Appendix B.5 adds in-house pretraining data and evaluations on DROP, BBH, C-Eval, TriviaQA, MMLU-Pro, AGIEval, Ape210K, GSM8K and MATH. This substantially broadens reasoning, knowledge and mathematics coverage while retaining the earlier CFG and OLMo evaluations.

E2.justification: The existing standard-model, MTP and MTP-DS comparisons are retained. Added experiments apply the existing baseline-versus-OE comparison to new model configurations; newly cited methods such as N-grammer are not evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: The new in-house experiment uses 400M activated parameters, 4B sparse parameters, a 36M OE vocabulary, 600B training tokens and few-shot evaluation. Section 4.4 adds matched-hardware throughput comparisons and inference tests with sequence length 2048 and batch sizes 1, 8 and 64. These are added protocols, not revisions to the retained experiments.

E4.justification: Section 4.4 adds supplementary efficiency analysis examining overhead across model scales, batch sizes, and prefill versus decoding. The vocabulary-scaling, hierarchical-embedding, hashing-conflict and OD-loss-weight ablations remain unchanged.

E5.justification: v2 adds no repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals or formal significance tests. Existing curve-smoothing and statistical reporting practices are retained.

E6.justification: New Tables 6-8 report throughput and computational costs, including training slowdowns of 4.63% and 8.3%. Table 9 adds baseline/OE scores such as TriviaQA 39.7/49.0 and GSM8K 40.6/46.2. These are additional results under new settings; existing Tables 1-5 and the OD table, renumbered from 6 to 10, retain their values.

T1.justification: Equation (5) changes the summand's argument from x^(-n) to x^(-i), correcting the hierarchical sum to use the corresponding i-gram input. The remaining mathematical formulation and Appendix C loss-decomposition derivation are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the claims about input-vocabulary scaling, log-linear loss reduction, low computational overhead and combining OE with OD. New experiments support these claims without redefining the main contributions.

C2.justification: Section 4.4 attributes runtime overhead mainly to communication, discusses MoE memory-access bottlenecks, and acknowledges insufficient optimization of the OLMoE-7B configuration. Appendix B.5 adds the interpretation that OE particularly benefits knowledge and improves in-context learning.

D1.justification: v2 specifies 32/64 A100 GPUs for the training-speed comparisons and single-A100 inference using Transformers with OE embeddings offloaded to CPU. It also documents the new in-house model configuration and training budget, although corpus composition and exact few-shot counts remain unspecified.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds discussion or citations covering lookup-table RNNs, N-grammer, Infini-gram, CANINE, Charformer and earlier multi-token prediction work. Section 3.2 explicitly credits Huang et al. and Roy et al. for prior n-gram hashing, refining attribution within the retained research framing.

P1.justification: v2 adds Sections 4.4 and B.5, acknowledgements and an impact statement, while retaining most existing prose and section order. Local edits include a shortened Section 2.3 heading, affiliation updates and repair of the unresolved Figure 13 reference.

P2.justification: Tables 6-9 are added, Figure 1 gains comparison and loss annotations, and existing figures and tables are repositioned within conference formatting. The former Table 6 becomes Table 10; Figures 2-14 retain their content.

improvement.justification: Measured training and inference costs and broader few-shot evaluations make the efficiency and applicability claims better supported. Improved prior-work attribution and the Equation (5) correction also help. The gains are limited by underspecified in-house data and few-shot protocols, while the unchanged 'no additional cost' wording remains insufficiently qualified given Table 6's reported 4.63% and 8.3% training overhead.
